patch.value: pm-ado: Azure DevOps work-item sync designed around revision-checked writes

Azure DevOps is the one major tracker whose write API is natively conflict-aware. Work items are updated with a JSON Patch document, and that document may carry a test operation asserting the current System.Rev. If another writer moved the item first the whole patch is rejected atomically instead of silently overwriting. That is a compare-and-swap on a remote tracker, and it is the primitive this ecosystem already organises itself around for multi-agent work. Every other integration in this fleet performs last-write-wins updates and can lose a concurrent edit; pm-ado does not have to, so every remote write asserts a revision.

Three further Azure DevOps capabilities map onto pm primitives more directly than Jira or Linear can express: System.Rev with its revisions endpoint is an append-only log on the remote side that can be reconciled against a pm item history rather than flattened into one updated_at; work item relations are typed and align with pm parent and dependency kinds instead of needing an ad hoc convention; and the work item batch endpoint accepts up to two hundred sub-requests per call, so a project sync costs a handful of round trips rather than hundreds, which is directly an agent's latency and token budget.

Every remote write carries a revision assertion, proven by a test that interleaves two writers and asserts the loser fails; work item revisions reconcile with pm item history; typed relations round-trip to pm parent and dependency kinds; a full project sync uses the batch endpoint and its request count is asserted; the credential preflight aborts before any store read or network call; coverage is 100 across statements, branches, functions and lines and the docstring gate passes

value.text: Audit 2026-09-13: EXISTS — revision assertions on every write (pm-ado-8zx9 closed; buildUpdatePatch leads with test /rev, assertsRevision guard in AdoClient); batch endpoint for project sync (pm-ado-ntkc closed; BATCH_LIMIT=200, batchIds); credential preflight aborts before network (shouldFailFast, runCredentialPreflight); 130 tests pass. REMAINS — work item revisions do not reconcile with pm item history (no revisions-endpoint reading or history reconciliation code); typed relations round-trip is half done (pm-ado-1zuu still open: ADO-to-pm mapping only, no reverse write, no cycle refusal). The epic cannot close until pm-ado-1zuu and the revisions-to-history reconciliation are done.
